exposure: mode of birth (Cesarean section, Normal Vaginal Delivery)
maternal history of urinary tract infection
cohort: The study included 92 newborn babies born between 37 and 41 weeks of gestation, from whom umbilical cord blood was collected immediately after birth.
finding: Neonatal cord blood thiol levels were significantly lower in both the Cesarean section group compared to the Normal Vaginal Delivery group, and in newborns of mothers with a history of urinary tract infection.
mod_finding: Neonatal cord blood thiol levels were significantly lower in the Cesarean section group compared to the Normal Vaginal Delivery group.
